name: Relativistic Antenna
description: Dipole Antenna driven harder: the charge swings in place, 7.3 units either side of the center, at up to 0.69 c (c = 1, Minkowski metric). The arrows show its Liénard–Wiechert field on a resting test charge (retarded: read on the light cone), travelling out at c in bands that reverse every half wavelength and repeat every wavelength (c·T = 60). While the charge moves fast, the 1/κ³ factor (κ = 1 − n·β) beams its radiation toward the way it moves, forward on one stroke and back on the next: averaged over a period it still vanishes along the axis of motion, but the lobes lean toward the axis and peak about 40° from it, not across it as in a slow antenna's sin²θ. The drive F0·cos(2πt/T) repeats every T = 60 (120 steps); the charge starts at the left end of its swing with u = −F0·dt/2, which cancels the half-step lead of the Euler kicks, so it never drifts. The drive comes from the fixed source far below the view (n = 1) and acts only on the charge with q2 = 1. Beyond c·(K − 1)·dt the charge's motion would be extrapolated uniformly from its oldest stored step; the view stays inside.

forces.name: Drive
forces.expression: n_j * q2_i * vec(F0 * cos(2 * pi * time / T), 0, 0)
